quality_gate.reason: 9 items are accepted for reviewed/caveat_only, but L03, L10 and L11 still need CEK-TA internal schemas/taxonomies before reviewed/caveat_only.

reasons: NIST least privilege、SEC market access controls、CME pre-trade risk sources support the reviewed/caveat-only boundary that live API permissions must be least-privilege and separated by capability.
The claim remains tool/broker-specific and does not prescribe a universal permission matrix or any trading action.

source: NIST/SEC/CME/IBKR support principles and implementation context only; broker/venue-specific permission mapping is still required.
content: State as a permission and governance boundary, not as a universal broker permission template.
boundary: No approved/default/hard gate; no trade execution advice; no account/key configuration recommendations.
conflict: Live Execution owns real API/session permissions; AI Engineering may only cite this as a readiness check.

reasons: FIX Execution Report and OrdStatus sources support formal order state semantics; IBKR callbacks support broker-specific lifecycle implementation examples.
The candidate does not create a universal exchange state machine; it only requires explicit state mapping and reconciliation state handling.

source: FIX/FIX dictionary and IBKR are semantic sources; native adapter mapping remains required per venue/broker.
content: Keep submitted/accepted/partial/filled/cancel/reject/expired/unknown/reconciliation_required as CEK-TA logical states, not guaranteed native labels.
boundary: No hard gate or live order action is created by this reviewed/caveat item.
conflict: Replay may simulate states; Live Execution owns real state truth and adapter mapping.

reasons: IBKR position/account sources support the need for position updates and reconciliation, but reviewed/caveat-only requires an internal CEK-TA position_reconciliation schema.

The package does not define required fields such as local_position_ref, broker_position_ref, account_statement_ref, discrepancy_type, mismatch_qty, mismatch_notional, stale_source, reconciliation_action, owner and audit_trace.
required_followups: Upload or inline CEK-TA position_reconciliation contract/schema.
Define source priority, reconciliation cadence, mismatch classification, missing-source handling, and what reconciliation_required permits or forbids.
Clarify owner split: Live Execution owns real account/broker position truth; Risk may consume reconciliation status but does not own broker truth.

source: Broker API docs support data availability, not the complete CEK-TA reconciliation field contract.
content: Add required/optional field table, mismatch taxonomy, source priority and stale/unknown handling.
boundary: reconciliation_required is evidence/control state, not automatic trade advice or risk threshold recommendation.
conflict: Must align with Data Engineering lineage, Live Execution account truth and Risk Management final gate consumption.

reasons: CME Kill Switch and pre-trade risk sources support order-entry block and cancellation controls; FIA/SEC support automated-trading safeguard context.
The candidate correctly frames kill switch as execution safety control, not strategy judgment.

source: CME/FIA/SEC are venue/regulatory/industry examples; external projects need their own broker/venue mapping.
content: Keep kill switch, order-entry block, cancel working orders, manual override and recovery as control capabilities.
boundary: Reviewed/caveat-only does not enable actual kill switch operation or hard gate authority.
conflict: Live Execution owns kill/cancel implementation; Risk owner defines policy and escalation.

reasons: IBKR/Binance/FIX/SEC sources support that live adapters must handle API behavior, order validation constraints, rejects and status outcomes explicitly.
The reviewed/caveat-only claim is limited to requiring structured error contracts; it does not prescribe a universal error-code taxonomy.
required_followups: Before approved-level materialization, add CEK-TA adapter_error_contract schema with retryability, severity, source, recoverability and owner fields.

source: External broker/exchange docs are implementation examples; they do not replace a project-specific adapter error taxonomy.
content: Structured errors must distinguish network, auth, rate-limit, validation, risk reject, unknown state and missing execution report.
boundary: No string exception may drive live decisioning; no execution action is authorized by this knowledge item.
conflict: Adapter error truth belongs to Live Execution; Risk consumes normalized risk-relevant errors.

reasons: FIX Execution Report, CME audit trail and IBKR callback sources support auditable records for orders, fills, rejects, cancels, fees and state changes.
The candidate remains a logging/audit boundary and does not include account facts or private strategy parameters.

source: FIX/CME/IBKR support order/fill/status/audit semantics; project schema still maps physical log fields.
content: Logs must link decision, order request, broker response, fill, reject/cancel, fee, slippage, risk trigger and manual action.
boundary: Auditability does not imply live permission or strategy validity.
conflict: Live Execution owns real execution logs; Risk owns risk-trigger logs; Backtest/Replay may reference but not overwrite.

reasons: SEC 15c3-5, CFTC 17 CFR 1.11, CME pre-trade controls and FIA guidance support pre-trade controls for order size/capital/credit/volume risk.
The candidate properly avoids numeric thresholds; thresholds must remain project-owner policy.

source: Regulatory/industry sources support risk-control principle, not CEK-TA threshold values.
content: Single-trade risk checks should be expressed as required policy fields, not values.
boundary: No risk threshold advice; no hard gate activation in this audit result.
conflict: Risk Management owns policy; Live Execution enforces only after project-defined policy is configured.

reasons: SEC/CFTC/CME/FIA sources support loss/capital controls as a risk-management boundary.
The claim is acceptable as caveat-only because it requires definition of loss basis, reset timezone, freeze and recovery flow without providing threshold numbers.
required_followups: Before approved/default use, add a daily_loss_policy schema with realized/unrealized basis, reset timezone, freeze state, manual recovery and owner fields.

source: External sources support the control principle but not project-specific daily-loss policy values.
content: Treat trigger threshold as a project-owned placeholder, not a recommended number.
boundary: No threshold advice; no live stop command is created by this reviewed/caveat item.
conflict: Risk owner defines policy; Live Execution enforces configured state only.

reasons: SEC/CFTC/CME/FIX sources support pre-trade limits and order/quantity state control.

boundary: No risk threshold numbers; no actual hard gate is enabled.

boundary: No threshold advice; no live stop command; caveat-only only.
